en.askTitle: Change the boxes to your own freelance setup and get the same structure and USD-receiving comparison before you start invoicing
en.runTitle: Florianópolis, Brazil: a freelance UX designer invoicing two US clients in USD

fields.label: Receiving routes to compare
fields.value: Wise Business, Payoneer, a Brazilian bank’s international transfer, and other well-documented options

en.template: Help me set up USD invoicing from Brazil. I am a {profession} in {city}, with {clients} clients in {country} paying about {amount} a month, starting on {start}. Compare MEI, an ME under Simples Nacional and working as an individual for my case, check whether my work counts under fator R (Annex III or V), and compare the cost of receiving USD through {routes} using my own quotes. Rebuild the monthly take-home with my pro-labore, accountant fee and exchange rate, and list what to ask my accountant. Flag anything unconfirmed. Ask before contacting anyone or paying anything.

phases.title: Research the Brazilian tax rules, receiving fees and accountant prices, then write and check the guide
phases.note: Structure and tax rules, fees for receiving USD, and accountant costs
phases.judgment: What it could not confirm is labelled, not filled in: the bank rows use illustrative 1–3% spreads rather than published fees, and Wise’s USD-to-BRL fee is a proxy marked unconfirmed. A second pass then recomputed 61 money figures and found 0 mismatches, after fixing 1-centavo rounding differences and a reversed range.

workers: Read the official Brazilian sources on MEI, Simples Nacional sign-up timing, minimum wage, social-security contributions and income tax, and listed what it could not find
Priced the ways to receive USD (Wise, Payoneer, PayPal, Remessa Online and bank transfers) against the official exchange rate for the worked examples
Collected published monthly prices from online accountants, plus digital-certificate costs, with the date each was read
